posts.text:
Three Russian objects violated Polish airspace early this morning as Russia launched a massive attack on Ukraine.

According to Polish Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, one was a Kh-101 missile, the second was also believed to be a missile, and the third was most likely a jet-powered drone.

"We are dealing with yet another provocation by Russia. I don't think the timing is a coincidence. The Coalition of the Willing is holding military exercises today," he added.

Air raid alerts were issued in Poland’s Lublin and Podkarpackie regions early this morning. Polish fighter jets were scrambled.

An unidentified object fell in a field near the village of Nowy Lipowiec in the Lublin region and caught fire, Polish police reported. The head of Biłgoraj County, Andrzej Szarlip, said that an explosion had occurred. Earlier, a video reportedly showing an explosion near the village of Chmielek in Biłgoraj County was posted online.

Dariusz Działo, head of the Security and Crisis Management Department at the Lublin Voivodeship Office, said the object was still burning, making it difficult for investigators to approach.

Polish police confirmed that another unidentified object fell in a wooded area near the town of Rudnik nad Sanem in the Podkarpackie region. Infrastructure Minister Dariusz Klimczak said that around 6:48 a.m., a railway dispatcher heard a loud bang near the tracks close to Rudnik nad Sanem. An initial inspection found no visible damage to the railway infrastructure. Rail traffic across the Podkarpackie region was suspended until 7:33 a.m., while services on line 068 (Nisko - Rudnik nad Sanem - Łętownia) were temporarily suspended for further inspections.

Due to the aerial threat, the Polish Air Navigation Services Agency evacuated the control tower at Rzeszów-Jasionka Airport. Nine people, including six operational staff members, took shelter during the alert.

PM Donald Tusk said that there was no doubt that the objects that landed in Poland were Russian.

"It seems we are dealing with an intentional provocation," he added.
